title: Customer network safe-mode, recovery, and audit retention — PRD draft
content:
Summary:

This is an early PRD sketch for a customer-network "safe-mode" and associated audit-retention / reconciliation workflows. Goal: provide a deterministic, operator-friendly way to automatically put a customer-managed networking surface into a degraded-but-safe state when we detect divergent telemetry (connectivity blips, missing approvals, or partial audit export failures), and to ensure audit evidence for those events is retained or reconcilable in low-bandwidth/offline scenarios.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Private deployments: customers manage portions of networking (firewalls, transit, NAT), but Redwood must preserve operational correctness and provide examplar audit evidence on incidents.
- Common failure modes: intermittent egress blocking causing incomplete audit forwarders, transient approval service outages, and asymmetric request success across regions.
- Existing options are binary: full fail-open or fail-closed. Teams want a middle state that preserves safety while keeping the model endpoints available in a limited capacity.
- Audit telemetry is costly to store indefinitely; customers sometimes run with intermittent connectivity and need a reconciliation path for sparse logs.

Goals (what success looks like):
1) Introduce a "safe-mode thermostat" that automatically reduces networking surface area and model capabilities (e.g., disables remote model fallback, restricts outbound telemetry) when defined signals exceed thresholds.
2) Guarantee an immutable audit bundle is produced for any safe-mode transition with enough evidence to diagnose the cause and meet compliance requests (timeboxed minimal footprint).
3) Provide a reconciliation flow for offline operators to upload missing telemetry and reconcile tokenized audit bundles with the control plane.
4) Minimize customer-visible disruption: degraded features must be documented and surfaced via Console, CLI, and an emergency webhook.
5) Configurable retention/compaction presets for customers with limited storage/egress.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for full forensics workflows or SIEM export tooling.
- Not intended to solve permanent loss of data from customer-managed on-prem archives.

User personas:
- Platform SRE (customer-side): wants a safe, testable automation to reduce blast radius during net outages.
- Redwood on-call: needs quick access to immutable evidence and ability to request an upload/reconciliation from customer.
- Security & Compliance reviewer: requires tamper-evident proof that can be inspected later.

Signals that trigger safe-mode (examples):
- Audit-forwarder heartbeat missing for > 3m and audit queue depth > X (X configurable),
- Approval-gate service latency p50 > 2s and >10% error rate for 2m,
- Cross-region request divergence: majority of requests to a deployment succeed in us-west but fail in eu-central with identical inputs,
- Manual operator escalation via console or /safe-mode API.

Thermostat design (high level):
- Throttles: discrete knobs applied when entering safe-mode, applied in order of least-to-most-disruptive: 
  1) Disable non-essential outbound telemetry (telemetry -> local buffer + compressed bundle),
  2) Disable model fallback to external variants (keep local quantized model),
  3) Limit concurrency (token-budget per-second),
  4) Enter maintenance-only routing (only preauthorized client IP blocks allowed).
- Rules are applied atomically and recorded in the audit bundle with before/after config diffs.

Audit bundle and retention:
- For each safe-mode event, create a compact audit bundle that includes:
  - event metadata (timestamp, trigger signals, versioned knob diffs),
  - a short sampling of request/response pairs (configurable sample size),
  - signed manifests (HMAC/ecdsa) linking local evidence to control-plane checkpoints,
  - reconciliation hints (cursor offsets, sequence numbers).
- Retention presets: 
  - "Conservative" (default): keep full bundles for 90 days in control plane plus local encrypted cache for 30 days,
  - "Compact": keep manifests + sample for 30 days, local compressed bundle for 7 days,
  - "Sparse" (low egress): keep only manifests and short fingerprints, expect customer to upload the full bundle during reconciliation windows.
- Bundles are immutable and have a canonical ID (sha256-based).

Offline reconciliation flow (operator experience):
1) Detection phase: control plane marks a reconciliation-needed state and surfaces instructions in Console and emergency webhook.
2) Customer collects local encrypted bundle (via agent/CLI) and pushes to an S3-compatible endpoint or uses console upload.
3) Control plane verifies signature and sequence continuity, then re-hydrates missing telemetry and completes audit index.
4) Post-reconciliation: system validates that tokens/requests reconcile to expected counts and emits a reconciliation report (signed).

Operational APIs and console UX: (rough)
- GET /v1/private/safe-mode/status -> shows current mode, active knobs, bundle IDs, trigger reasons, elapsed time.
- POST /v1/private/safe-mode/ack -> operator can acknowledge and provide optional friction text (reason, contact).
- POST /v1/private/reconcile/uploads -> accepts signed bundle upload with metadata.
- Console: timeline view for each deployment showing safe-mode entries, ability to download signed bundle, one-click request to customer with prefilled upload instructions.

Security and tamper-evidence:
- Bundle signing: agent signs with device key (customer-managed or Redwood ephemeral key), control plane records signed checkpoint.
- Replay resistance: sequence numbers + checkpoint hash chain ensure missing chunk detection.
- Minimal PII: bundles must default-redact content; samples are sanitized unless customer opts-in.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiment): run safe-mode thermostat in read-only observability mode for small set of opt-in pilots (internal teams + 3 customers) — 6 weeks.
- Phase 1 (conservative default): enable safe-mode with Conservative retention in Dedicated deployments behind feature flag — 8–10 weeks.
- Phase 2 (operator tooling): add reconciliation UI, signer key management, and compressed-bundle CLI — 6 weeks.
- Phase 3 (GA): support presets and SLA-backed retention tiers for Dedicated/Private customers.

Metrics to evaluate:
- Number of safe-mode activations per month (by trigger type),
- Mean time to reconcile (customer upload -> control plane completion),
- Fraction of activations with completed signed bundle within 72 hours,
- Customer-reported severity/regression post-safe-mode.

Engineering constraints / dependencies:
- Requires small agent change to produce signed compact bundles and local compressed cache.
- Control plane storage for bundles + index (capacity planning needed).
- Approval-gate and telemetry subsystems must emit additional debug trace IDs to be included in bundles.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Default throttle order: should we ever allow skipping funnel stages for high-security customers? (need policy matrix)
- Egress cost: compressed bundles can still be large — should Redwood provide a managed upload proxy (proxying to S3) for low-egress customers?
- Signing key model: customer-provided keys vs ephemeral Redwood keys — tradeoff between usability and cryptographic assurances.
- Data privacy: how strict should default redaction be? Will heavy redaction reduce postmortem value?

Next steps (short list):
- Sync with serving-runtime (agent binary change) to outline minimal bundle format (deadline: 2025-11-10),
- Sketch console timeline UI and pre-approved operator email templates (OWNER: Lena),
- Draft a security-approved signing/key rotation playbook (OWNER: Ethan),
- Create pilot list (3 customers + internal SRE) and target pilot start 2025-12-01.

Notes / random ideas to capture:
- "Safe-mode thermostat" name came from ops brainstorming — we might rename to "network safe-mode" or "operational thermostat".
- Consider a "reconciliation escrow" where incomplete bundles are persisted in a short-term escrow for 14 days to simplify customer uploads.
- For low-bandwidth customers, a bittorrent-like partial-sync could be useful but is out of scope for MVP.

Raw sample audit manifest (toy):
- id: sha256:abc123...,
- timestamp: 2025-10-30T02:14:09Z,
- trigger: audit-forwarder-heartbeat-missing,
- knob-diff: {telemetry:off, fallback:disabled, concurrency:50%},
- samples: [request-snips],
- signature: ecdsa:0xdeadbeef...

If this resonates, I can convert into a more formal PRD layout (acceptance criteria, UX mockups, API contract) and split into separate engineering tickets for agent, control-plane indexer, and Console UI.

— Priya
